source.publication: 2025 Form 80-100 Resident, Non-Resident and Part-Year Resident Individual Income Tax Instructions (Rev. 12/25) and the 2025 Form 80-105 Resident Return (Rev. 09/25)
source.section: Form 80-105 page 1 lines 8-17 and page 2 lines 38-66; Instructions PDF p.5 Filing Status and Exemptions table; p.6 Additional Exemptions, Lines 8-12; p.7 Lines 14-17; p.22 Tax Rates; p.27 Schedule of Tax Computation lines 1-4; Instructions PDF p.11 Line 40 ('All income is taxed at the same rate'), Line 44; FAQ 'What is the Mississippi tax treatment of long-term capital gains?'

worked: Federal AGI = wages (person 0) 30,000.00 + dividends 5,000.00 + short-term gains 2,000.00 + long-term gains 20,000.00 = 57,000.00. Federal taxable income = 57,000.00 - 15,750.00 federal standard deduction = 41,250.00 (given, not tested; the federal senior deduction is ignored). Form 80-105 filing status box 5, Single. Start at federal AGI 57,000.00 (Mississippi builds its own income on lines 38 to 66; the projection starts from federal AGI and takes out the exempt income, the same result here). Line 66 and line 13 Mississippi AGI = 57,000.00. Line 14 standard deduction 2,300.00. Line 8 age boxes checked 0; line 10 = 0 x 1,500.00 = 0.00; line 11 6,000.00; line 12 and line 15 = 6,000.00. Line 16 Mississippi taxable income = 57,000.00 - 2,300.00 - 6,000.00 = 48,700.00. Schedule of Tax Computation line 1: first 10,000.00 x 0% = 0.00; line 2: remaining 38,700.00 x 4.4% = 1,702.80; line 4 and line 17 = 1,702.80. Lines 18 and 19 credits 0.00; line 20 = 1,702.80. The form rounds to whole dollars (p.22), which would give 1,703; expected keeps the formula result. No special rate. The narrow exemption for shares in Mississippi financial institutions and domestic ownership interests is not modelled, so all gains are taxed.
accepted_approximations: Mississippi builds its own income (Form 80-105 lines 38 to 66); the projection starts from federal AGI and removes the exempt income through the reliefs and Social Security treatment.

Gains exempted on shares in financial institutions domiciled in Mississippi and on domestic corporation or partnership interests held more than one year; a projection cannot tell these from other gains, which are taxable.
